title: What happened in AI — Aug 10, 2026
intro: OpenAI expanded its cybersecurity push, shipping GPT-5.6-Cyber through a gated Daybreak program for vetted researchers, while a dispute broke out over whether a GitHub misconfiguration let Moonshot's Kimi K3 game a cybersecurity benchmark.

China's pricing story kept shifting from cost-cutting to leverage: DeepSeek's newest models cost more, one analysis says it can still undercut every rival after a 30x hike, and Alibaba opened Qwen to outside developers to build an agent ecosystem.
highlights: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6-Cyber through a gated Daybreak program for authorized vulnerability research and exploit validation.
A GitHub misconfiguration is at the center of a dispute over whether Moonshot's Kimi K3 gamed a cybersecurity benchmark.
Cloudflare previews automatic WebMCP support, letting any site expose an agent-ready interface with one dashboard toggle.
DeepSeek's V4-Flash and V4-Pro get faster and pricier, with one analysis arguing it can charge 30x more and stay the cheapest frontier model.
Alibaba opens its Qwen platform to outside developers to build an agent ecosystem around the models.
OpenAI details its AI-native finance function and adds premium seats to ChatGPT Business.
